summary: The Solana version is built and has passed local tests and independent reviews. It is waiting for your approval to start a roughly six-week trial on Solana’s public test network; nothing has been deployed there. A separate fix for the existing rewards system is tested locally, but live changes and repayments remain held.

glossary.definition: Milestone 14: the planned trial on Solana’s public test network. Earlier milestones established local implementation and test evidence; this trial has not started.

The proposed Solana test-network work: fresh test keys, free test tokens, program and governance setup, then the scheduled acceptance tests. It excludes Internet Computer changes, real reward issuance, the main network and merging the code.
Solana’s public network for testing. Its test tokens come from a faucet and are not real main-network funds.
A service that gives out free test-network tokens for the planned trial.
The address identifying the Solana program. Using a fresh address changes related derived addresses and requires updated build references and local review.
The exact changed source, compiled program, interface and derived addresses are recorded again so reviewers can identify what would be used.
A recorded fingerprint and code revision identifying exact approval-packet bytes. It proves which document was used, not that Rob approved it.
The local Solana execution environment used to run the compiled program in tests without publishing it to a public network.
The external randomness provider selected for the game’s draws. Local tests used its actual program with simulated conditions; real public-network fulfilment remains untested.
Verifiable random function: the randomness mechanism used by the selected provider for game draws.
Version 4 of the Solana multisignature program used for shared governance. Local compatibility tests ran its actual compiled program.
An account requiring multiple designated approvals before it can carry out a governed action.
The separate test account whose signature and funding are required for program initialization; tests checked that its signature survives the governance execution path.
The chosen order and timing of the acceptance tests. The local time-advanced simulation reached all 39 steps; running the same schedule normally takes about six weeks.
The local test clock was advanced artificially so time-dependent scenarios could be tested without waiting six actual weeks.
Checks that the program’s money-accounting totals still balance after each tested step.
Labels for the acceptance scenarios the plan requires. Reaching all of them in a local simulation does not prove a public-network run.
Inspect or simulate a proposed action without sending its transaction. For board publication, compare the local projection with the saved board without uploading an update.
A Solana node. The reported real-node tests used an isolated local node, not the public test network.
Repeating an operation produces no extra effect. The reviewed funding guards also prevent another payment after an earlier payment is confirmed.
The network’s starting identifier, checked to help ensure the tool targets the intended Solana network.
The production network where real activity and funds exist; the proposed test-network approval does not include it.
The reviewer completed the stated review and found issues. This label alone does not mean the issues are fixed or execution is approved.
The numbered findings from the first operator-tool review. These are review issue labels, not releases or acceptance-flow numbers.

In this operator-tool review, the unknown-transaction-outcome problem: a missing lookup after expiry could allow a transfer that already happened to be repeated. The narrow repair is accepted locally.
The four residual findings from the second operator-tool review: read commitment, safe resume, durable journal handling and recording the packet fingerprint.
The reviewer’s severity label for the misconfigured post-send reads. It describes that specific review finding, not the project’s overall readiness.
The Solana confirmation level requested when reading state. The repair prevents those reads silently using a different level.
A stronger Solana confirmation level. The earlier configuration error caused reads to wait for this level unintentionally.
The transaction’s recent-network reference has become too old for new processing. This does not establish whether the transaction already succeeded earlier.
The tool saves a durable transaction record before sending, so a restart cannot silently forget that it may already have acted.
The tool cannot establish whether a transaction happened. It blocks execution and keeps the original transaction record; it does not assume failure or automatically retry.
A check using recorded transaction outcomes to stop another funding transfer after one is confirmed. Unresolved transactions remain held.
A reviewer other than the implementer inspected the scoped repair and its evidence. Codex inspected the source and regression assertions without rerunning the coordinator’s tests.
A test designed to catch an earlier bug returning. Here, the tests assert that lost responses and missing status information cause no additional payment.
A searchable map connecting source files, concepts and documents. It helps navigation; it does not prove the program ran correctly.
Individual entries in the knowledge map, such as files or concepts.
Connections grouping several related knowledge-map entries together.
A digital fingerprint identifying exact file contents. Matching a hash identifies bytes, not approval, deployment or successful operation.
A saved record of what was observed or completed. Its meaning depends on the operation: a board-publication receipt is not evidence of a game transaction.
Read the saved result again and compare it with the expected version.
A sanitized copy of selected canonical-board information for display in Lookout. The repository board remains authoritative.
The publisher was switched to read the durable project-owned projection file instead of the initial temporary copy.
Pull request: a proposed set of code changes for review. An open draft is not a merge or a deployment.
Continuous integration: automated build and test checks run by the code-hosting service. Their result must be checked for the exact code revision.
Internet Computer, the network hosting the existing application and reward services. Its deployment approvals remain separate from the Solana trial.
The existing project reward token or points. Issuing real rewards is separate from the Solana test-network work.
The existing reward service containing the separately scoped ledger-memo repair.
An extra note attached to a token-ledger operation. The existing ledger limits its length; this repair preserves short notes and fingerprints longer ones.
The local compatibility check says the proposed service update can preserve the existing stored-state format. It does not prove a live upgrade occurred.
A test on a local Internet Computer environment that reproduced the old failure, applied the update and checked subsequent operations.
The separate question of recovering missed historical rewards. Claim coverage and duplicate prevention must be established before any repayment decision.
Ten checks passed out of ten in the named local oracle-compatibility suite; this is not ten public-network transactions.
Twelve checks passed out of twelve in the local compatibility suite that ran the actual Squads v4 program; these are not public-network transactions.
Twelve local flow-runner checks passed out of twelve after the review fixes; the runner has not run on the public test network.
Twelve local flow-runner checks passed out of twelve at that earlier repair stage; a historical local result.
Thirty local tool checks passed at an earlier repair stage. Those historical results were later qualified by the additional unknown-outcome finding.

Thirty local tool checks passed at an earlier repair stage. Those historical results were later qualified by the additional unknown-outcome finding, which has since been repaired and accepted locally.
All 145 local unit checks passed for the separate legacy memo repair.
All 29 checks passed in the legacy repair’s local upgrade rehearsal; no live update is implied.
